headline: Sox Drop Another Tough One In Tampa As Bats Remain Cold
morning_brew: Another night down in Tampa, another frustrating result that makes you want to chuck your remote. The Sox dropped a tough four to three contest to the Rays on Tuesday, making it three straight road losses. Payton Tolle took the loss on the mound, grinding through six innings but letting up four earned runs on nine hits. We clawed back with two runs in the eighth, but the mountain was just too high to climb.

This team is now sitting at twenty-seven wins and thirty-eight losses, still stuck in the basement of the American League East. Are you kiddin' me with this? The bats are just completely frozen. Both Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela went zero for four on the night, leaving way too many guys stranded. Wilyer Abreu picked up a hit, but one knock from your key outfielders is not going to get the job done when you are chasing the top teams in the division.

Down in Foxborough, at least we have some positive vibes to keep us going through the summer heat. The connection between Drake Maye and his new weapon A.J. Brown is reportedly growing by the day during these mandatory minicamp sessions. Coming off that tough Super Bowl loss to Seattle, building this chemistry early is exactly what this offense needs. Having a true number one threat like Brown out there should make life a whole lot easier for our young quarterback when the real action starts in September.
